newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven says won't take up stock in MGM IPO.
newsitem.headline: Seven says won't take up stock in MGM IPO.

text.p: Television operator Seven Network Ltd said on Wednesday it did not intend to take up any stock in Metro-Goldwyn Mayer Inc's proposed public offer of shares.
Seven said the shares would be offered by P & F Acquisition Corp, the entity through which Seven Network holds its investments in the movie studio.

"Seven Network Limited does not intend taking up any stock in the initial public offer (IPO) and, if the IPO proceeds, all stock currently held by Seven Network Limited will rank pari passu with P & F's common voting stock," Seven said.
P & F will be publicly listed which will enable the value of the investment to be more readily assessable, the television operator said.
Seven said it was not presently in a position to advise the offer price or the number of shares to be offered by P & F or the potential dilution effect of this on Seven's investment.
Last October, Seven joined up with U.S. billionaire Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp to acquire MGM for U$1.3 billion.
Last month, the new MGM owners completed a $573 million acquisition of Orion Corp and Goldwyn Entertainment Co, adding to MGM's large film library and its slate of movies in production.

Sources close to MGM said the Hollywood studio, which is led by chairman and chief executive officer Frank Mancuso, is looking to raise about $250 million, or about 12.5 percent of the company's total equity.

Funds raised from the MGM float would be used for film and television production and to help support operations of other company divisions, but would not be used to pay down debt incurred in the acquisition, sources said.
MGM said in a statement issued in Los Angles that all the shares issued would be new shares, and funds would be used for general corporate purposes.

Seven said it was prohibited from making any statements in relation to the IPO, either verbally or in writing, until after registration of the prospectus. At 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT), Seven shares were steady at A$5.70. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
